_readme: MONEY-1359 — error-level log VOLUME for one service.
Deliberately a coarse instrument. It is not trying to find the bug; it is
trying to notice that a service started shouting, which nothing did before.
The per-service threshold is what makes that possible: stockbook-workers runs
~60 job routes and has a higher healthy floor than apps/api does.
`status:error` and not `level:error`. Pino emits the level as a LABEL (see
packages/logger/src/config.ts formatters.level) and the transport tags the
line `ddsource:nodejs`, so Datadog's nodejs integration pipeline remaps it to
the reserved `status` attribute. If that pipeline is ever absent this query
matches nothing — which is why apply-service-monitors.sh runs a search
PREFLIGHT and refuses the row rather than creating a monitor over an empty
query (MONEY-1362 owns the remapper if the preflight says it is missing).
name: [{{env}}] {{service}} — more than {{threshold}} error logs in an hour
message:
{{service}} logged more than {{threshold}} error-level lines in the last hour.

Logs: `service:{{service}} env:{{env}} status:error`, then group by `@msg` — a single repeated message is a different incident from a spread, and the shape tells you which before you read one line.

Redaction is CLIENT-SIDE and this alert does not change that: `packages/logger` redacts through pino serializers and `redact` paths, and workers additionally wrap `console.*` (MONEY-1209, after live NSE session cookies reached prod Cloud Logging). A credential visible in a sample here is a bug in that redaction, not a Datadog setting to change.

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: FALSE. Zero error logs in an hour is the outcome we WANT, and it is common.
A no-data notification here would page on the healthiest possible state,
which is the fastest way to have this channel muted (MONEY-1238).
'The service stopped logging entirely' is a real failure and is NOT this
monitor's question — the APM error-rate row and each job's zero-write monitor
_enable_logs_sample_rationale: TRUE, and it is the one option here worth arguing. Datadog attaches sample
log lines to the notification, so the alert arrives with evidence instead of
a count that sends you to a search box.
It is safe for the same reason the redaction paragraph above is in the
message: what reaches Datadog was already redacted before it left the
